what_its_for: Bosutinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of blood cancer called chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML). It works by blocking a protein that tells cancer cells to grow, which helps slow or stop the cancer from spreading.
how_to_take: Take bosutinib by mouth with food once a day. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep steady levels of the medicine in your body. If you vomit after taking your dose, do NOT take another dose that day — just wait until your next scheduled dose.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you, typically 400 mg to 500 mg taken once daily with food. Your dose may be adjusted depending on how your body responds to the medicine or if you have side effects. Always follow exactly what your doctor tells you — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember with food. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store bosutinib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired tablets safely — ask your pharmacist how to properly discard them.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking bosutinib, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), as it can make bosutinib less effective. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with bosutinib. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine — it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 30 days after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe tiredness; signs of fluid retention such as sudden weight gain, swelling of hands, feet, or face, or trouble breathing; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or sore throat; unusual bruising or bleeding; chest pain or irregular heartbeat; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face or throat. Regular blood tests will be needed to monitor your blood counts, kidney function, and liver health.
when_it_works: Bosutinib does not work overnight. It may take several weeks to months before your doctor sees improvement in your blood test results or cancer markers. Keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Do not use bosutinib if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can seriously harm the baby. Women of childbearing age must use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 30 days after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Kidney or Liver Problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or monitor you more closely. Always tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions before starting this medicine. Elderly Patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially fluid retention and digestive issues. Report any new or worsening symptoms to your doctor promptly.
